guitar.evidence: Brian May's homemade "Red Special" guitar is one of the most iconic and well-documented instruments in rock history.

tone.target: clean arpeggios into bright classic-rock crunch
tone.profile: clean arpeggios into bright classic-rock crunch
tone.summary: A dynamic chain starting with light compression for clarity, followed by a versatile pre-amp boost. The core tone uses the UK 45 or US Deluxe amp model paired with a 4x12 cabinet to handle both clean arpeggios and bright classic rock crunch.
corrections: use distinct clean and crunch scenes

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Smooth out clean arpeggios and add sustain.
Provide subtle boost for power chords and increase perceived volume.
Used for the hard-rock crunch section (optional/scene switch). Kept low to avoid metal gain.
blocks.gap: The Red Haze is better suited for fuzz, but its mild drive can simulate early breakup without excessive grit.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the Vox/Marshall clean-to-crunch tone required for classic rock.
Provide the classic British cabinet sound (Vox/Marshall feel).
Enhance the bright upper mids and clarity for arpeggios.
Used sparingly for subtle movement during clean sections (avoiding 'wash').
blocks.gap: The Chorus is generally avoided, but a very low setting can add dimension.

blocks.purpose: Provide the required short room reverb for depth without sounding overly wet.
Used for specific rhythmic accents or section transitions.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet IR to better capture the bright, open sound of a Vox/Marshall 4x12 while enhancing upper mids for arpeggios.

proposals.recommendedAsset: Vox AC30 or British Fender-style IR
proposals.reason: Enhance the bright, open sound and upper mids needed for clean arpeggios.
proposals.expectedGain: Increased clarity and definition in clean sections.
